content: 1. If medically necessary, administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. The use of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with other proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) has not been studied. Omeprazole reduces the absorption and effectiveness of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after a locally-acting antacid. 2. Omeprazole decreases the effectiveness of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, which may reduce sparsentan exposure and efficacy. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. PPIs may reduce sparsentan exposure, potentially compromising its therapeutic efficacy. 3. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 4. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid concurrent use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates, as even minimal changes in concentration may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate according to product labeling. 5. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Start abrocitinib at 50 mg once daily when co-administered with CYP2C19 inhibitors. If an adequate response is not achieved after 12 weeks, the dose may be increased to 100 mg once daily. Discontinue abrocitinib if the response remains inadequate after the dosage increase. 6. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of acebutolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 7. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of alendronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 8. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of allopurinol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 9. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of amantadine by altering urine pH to a more alkaline state, which may lead to amantadine accumulation and an increased risk of adverse reactions. Monitor for amantadine-related adverse effects. 10. Amobarbital reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of amphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor. Reduced gastric acidity caused by PPIs decreases the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine, although the area under the curve (AUC) remains unaffected. 12. Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Sodium bicarbonate also reduces the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. 13. Armodafinil increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of atenolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 15. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Omeprazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of azithromycin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 18. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of bearberry by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor. 19. Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with PPIs. 20. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of belzutifan by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Belzutifan is a CYP2C19 substrate, and co-administration with CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase the incidence or severity of adverse effects. Monitor for anemia and hypoxia, and reduce the belzutifan dose as recommended. 21. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of benazepril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of benzphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor. 23. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of betaxolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 24. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of bisoprolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 25. Bortezomib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Omeprazole reduces the levels of bosutinib by approximately 45% due to pH-dependent solubility. Use caution and monitor. PPIs may decrease bosutinib concentration, as bosutinib displays pH-dependent solubility. 27. Omeprazole reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution, potentially affecting drug release and absorption in the duodenum. 28. Butabarbital reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Butalbital reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Cannabidiol also increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates when co-administered with cannabidiol. 31. Omeprazole reduces the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH caused by PPI use may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and/or reduce absorption. 32. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of captopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Sodium bicarbonate may decrease the absorption of captopril. 33. Carbamazepine reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Omeprazole also reduces the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. 35. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of carvedilol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 36. Omeprazole reduces the effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 37. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 38. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 39. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Omeprazole also reduces the effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. 40. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of celecoxib by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 41. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Cenobamate also increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider a dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates when used concomitantly with cenobamate. 42. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of celiprolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 43. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of chenodiol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 44. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of chloroquine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 45. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. A large proportion of ciprofloxacin is excreted unchanged in the urine. When urinary alkalinizing agents such as sodium bicarbonate are used concomitantly, the solubility of ciprofloxacin can be decreased due to alkaline urine. Omeprazole also reduces the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. The absorption of ciprofloxacin extended-release tablets was slightly diminished (20%) when co-administered with omeprazole. 46. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. The maximum recommended dose of citalopram for patients taking CYP2C19 inhibitors is 20 mg/day due to the risk of QT prolongation. 47. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease the solubility of crizotinib and subsequently reduce its bioavailability. However, no formal studies have been conducted. 48. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of clobazam by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Dosage adjustment may be required, as CYP2C19 inhibitors may result in increased exposure to N-desmethylclobazam (an active metabolite). 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease the solubility of crizotinib and subsequently reduce its bioavailability. However, no formal studies have been conducted. 52. Omeprazole and cyclosporine may each increase the toxicity of the other through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Long-term use of PPIs may cause hypomagnesemia and increase this risk when co-administered with drugs that may also decrease magnesium levels. 53. Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that alter upper GI tract pH (e.g., PPIs, H2-blockers, antacids) may decrease dabrafenib solubility and reduce its bioavailability. Dabrafenib also reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use an alternative if available. 54. Deferoxamine reduces the levels of sodium bicarbonate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Deferoxamine chelates iron; its affinity for other minerals is unknown. 55. Sodium bicarbonate and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor. 56. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor. Reduced gastric acidity caused by PPIs decreases the time to Tmax for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine, although the AUC remains unaffected. 57. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of diazepam (buccal and intranasal forms) by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, thereby increasing adverse reactions to diazepam. 58. Dichlorphenamide and omeprazole both decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor. 59. Omeprazole increases the toxicity of digoxin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Prolonged use of PPIs may cause hypomagnesemia and increase the risk for digoxin toxicity. 60. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Efavirenz also reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. No dose adjustments are needed for omeprazole at 40 mg/day or less. Elagolix also reduces the levels of omeprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered. Consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. 62. Omeprazole increases the levels of eluxadoline by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
